newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie says Indocopper sale to boost net.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie says Indocopper sale to boost net.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers said on Thursday the sale of its 49-percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama would increase its 1997 net profit by around 170 billion rupiah.
"We expect to add 135 billion rupiah in net capital gains and 36 billion in net interest gains this year from the sale of PT Indocopper," Bakrie president-director Tanri Abeng told reporters.
PT Nusamba Mineral Industri announced on Wednesday a tender offer to buy a 50.479-percent stake in PT Indocopper for around $300 million.
PT Indocopper Investama Corp has a 9.36 percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in eastern Irian Jaya province.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States owns 81.28 percent of Freeport Indonesia, with the remaining 9.36 percent held by the Indonesian government.
Freeport McMoRan has a 49-percent stake in Indocopper, Bakrie & Brothers 49 percent before the sale, and Bakrie Investindo around 1.5-percent. The remaining shares are held by the public.
Tanri said Bakrie Investindo had also sold its stake in Indocopper to Nusamba. Investindo is not part of listed Bakrie & Brothers, but is part of the Bakrie Group.
Its financial results were not consolidated into Bakrie's financial results, he said. He declined to give further details on Investindo's stake sale in Indocopper.
Tanri said some 60 percent of the $302.65 million proceeds from the Indocopper sale would be used to pay off mostly short-term debt, while the remaining 40 percent would be used for investment.
Bakrie expected to use the proceeds for investment in its core businesses which include telecommunications, infrastructure and plantations, Tanri said.
He said that to boost its telecommunications business, Bakrie this year expected to further strengthen its Uzbekhistan's telecommunications venture and its radio telecommunication unit PT Ratelindo.

Bakrie planned to invest around 150 billion rupiah in the telecommunications business, 370 billion rupiah in its infrastructure division and 80 billion rupiah in plantations this year, he said. $1=2,373 rupiah
